2.text: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved friend and fellow laborer,

3.text: to the beloved Apphia, Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house:

4.text: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

5.text: I thank my God, making mention of you always in my prayers,

6.text: hearing of your love and faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,

7.text: that the sharing of your faith may become effective by the acknowledgment of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.

8.text: For we have great joy and consolation in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed by you, brother.

9.text: Therefore, though I might be very bold in Christ to command you what is fitting,

10.text: yet for love's sake I rather appeal to you--being such a one as Paul, the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ--

11.text: I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten while in my chains,

12.text: who once was unprofitable to you, but now is profitable to you and to me.

13.text: I am sending him back. You therefore receive him, that is, my own heart,

14.text: whom I wished to keep with me, that on your behalf he might minister to me in my chains for the gospel.

15.text: But without your consent I wanted to do nothing, that your good deed might not be by compulsion, as it were, but voluntary.

16.text: For perhaps he departed for a while for this purpose, that you might receive him forever,

17.text: no longer as a slave but more than a slave--a beloved brother, especially to me but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.

18.text: If then you count me as a partner, receive him as you would me.

19.text: But if he has wronged you or owes anything, put that on my account.

20.text: I, Paul, am writing with my own hand. I will repay--not to mention to you that you owe me even your own self besides.

21.text: Yes, brother, let me have joy from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in the Lord.

22.text: Having confidence in your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I say.

23.text: But, meanwhile, also prepare a guest room for me, for I trust that through your prayers I shall be granted to you.

24.text: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, greets you,

25.text: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow laborers.
